title: The Feast of Booths
lead: The fall harvest feast, when Israel lives seven days in booths to remember the wilderness (Leviticus 23:33–43). The prophets made it a picture of the nations worshiping God (Zechariah 14:16), and Jesus spoke of living water and light at the feast (John 7–8).

sections.b: Exodus calls it the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year (Exodus 23:16). Leviticus 23:39–43 commands booths and branches; Deuteronomy calls for joy with the poor and the foreigner and a reading of the law every seventh year (Deuteronomy 16:13–15; Deuteronomy 31:10–13). Solomon dedicated the Temple at this feast (1 Kings 8:2), and Ezra's people built booths for the first time since Joshua (Nehemiah 8:13–18). Zechariah sees all nations going up to keep it (Zechariah 14:16–19). At the feast Jesus cries, "If someone is thirsty, he should come to me" (John 7:37–38), and John says the Word "pitched his tent" among us (John 1:14).
